summary: California's 16th Congressional District spans parts of Santa Clara and San Mateo counties on the Peninsula and in the South Bay. Incumbent Democrat Sam Liccardo, the former San Jose mayor first elected in 2024, placed first in the June 2 primary with 75.6%; Republican Peter Soulé placed second with 10.8%, narrowly ahead of fellow Republican Kevin Johnson (10.2%).

positions.stance: Sits on the House Financial Services Committee, including its subcommittee on digital assets, financial technology, and AI. (Wikipedia)
'People need to feel safe in their neighborhoods. Current laws need to be enforced.' (Ballotpedia candidate survey)
Says California's economy is being 'strangled by excessive regulations and wasteful spending'. (Ballotpedia candidate survey)

key_differences: This is not a competitive seat: Liccardo took about three-quarters of the primary vote and had raised over $3.2 million by May 2026, while Soulé's reported fundraising was minimal.
Soulé runs on general public-safety and anti-regulation themes; this research found no detailed federal policy platform from him.
